title.en: Practice: Setting priorities and solving problems step by step
title.hi: अभ्यास: प्राथमिकताएँ तय करना और समस्या को चरण-दर-चरण हल करना

section: Practice (written by us, not from a UPSC paper): Setting priorities and solving problems step by step

en.stem: You reach your office at 9 a.m. and find four matters waiting. Which do you take up first?
options: A monthly report due at the end of the week
A request to speak at a function next month
A message that a wall of a school building in your area has cracked and classes begin at 10 a.m.
A file on next year's furniture purchase
en.why: Only the third matter carries a risk to safety, and it has one hour. Life and safety come first.

en.stem: A legal reply must reach the court by 5 p.m. today or the case goes by default. A visiting senior wants a briefing at 3 p.m. that could be given tomorrow. You have time to prepare only one properly. What do you do?
options: Prepare the briefing, since the senior is waiting
Complete the legal reply, and tell the senior the reason and ask to give the briefing tomorrow
en.why: Losing the case by default cannot be undone; a briefing can be moved. Rank of the person asking is not a test. The fourth option also tells the person affected.

en.stem: Which of the following is important but not urgent for the head of a town's water department in January?
options: Preparing the plan for supply in the coming summer
Repairing a main pipe that burst this morning
Answering a routine circular about stationery
en.why: The summer plan matters a great deal but nothing is lost today if it is done next week. The burst pipe is urgent and important.

en.stem: Ten field workers are waiting for your instructions to start a survey. You also have a two-hour note to write, due this evening. It is morning. What is the best order?
options: Write the note first, then instruct the workers
Instruct the workers first, then write the note
Ask the workers to come tomorrow
Ask a worker to write the note
en.why: Ten people are idle until instructed, and the note is not due until evening. The task on which others depend comes first.

en.stem: After a storm you have one repair team for the day. Which job should it do first?
options: A street light outside an office
The line to a block of twenty houses
The line to the district hospital, which is running on a generator with fuel for four hours
The line to a cinema hall
en.why: The hospital involves life, a short time limit and many vulnerable people. It ranks first on every test.

en.stem: You have forty minutes before a meeting. Three things are pending: (1) a two-minute call to confirm a vehicle for a medical team leaving in an hour; (2) reading a thirty-minute file for the meeting; (3) replying to routine mail. What is the best order?
en.why: The call is short, others depend on it, and it has a deadline. The file is needed for the meeting. Routine mail can wait.

en.stem: A senior officer's assistant telephones repeatedly to ask you to process a routine file out of turn. At the same time, pension papers of a retired employee, already delayed, need your signature today to be included in this month's payment. What do you do first?
options: Do neither until the calls stop
Ask the pensioner to come next month
en.why: The pension has a deadline today and affects a person with little power to help themselves. Repeated calls do not raise the priority of a routine file.

en.stem: Three officers, P, Q and R, are to be given three duties, one each: counter, field and records. P cannot do field duty. Q cannot do counter duty or field duty. Who does the counter duty?
en.why: Q can do only records. P cannot do field, and records is taken, so P does counter. R does field.

en.stem: Four jobs A, B, C and D are to be done one each day from Monday to Thursday. B must be done before C. D must be on Monday. A must be done after C. On which day is C done?
en.why: D is on Monday. The other three must run B, C, A in that order on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. So C is on Wednesday.

en.stem: A fund of 60 lakh rupees is to be divided among four villages. Village W must get 20 lakh. Villages X and Y must get equal amounts. Village Z must get 10 lakh. How much does X get?
en.why: W and Z take 30 lakh. The remaining 30 lakh is shared equally by X and Y, so each gets 15 lakh.

en.stem: A committee of three is to be chosen from five people: A, B, C, D and E. A and B cannot both be on it. If C is on it, D must also be on it. E must be on it. Which of the following is a possible committee?
en.why: The second and fourth have A and B together; the fourth also lacks E. The third has C without D. The first meets every condition.

en.stem: Using the conditions of the previous question (three from A, B, C, D, E; A and B not together; C needs D; E must be included), which of the following must be true?
options: B is not on the committee
en.why: With E fixed, two more are needed from A, B, C and D. A and B cannot both be chosen, so at least one place goes to C or D, and C cannot come without D. The possible committees are A D E, B D E and C D E. D is in all three. Each of the other statements fails in at least one of them.

en.stem: Five files are to be cleared in order of priority. File P concerns a payment to a hospital supplier who will stop supplies tomorrow if unpaid. File Q is an annual report due in ten days. File R is leave for an employee from next week. File S is a reply to a court due in three days. File T is a proposal for a staff picnic. Which should be cleared first?
en.why: File P has the nearest deadline and touches patient care. File S is next, with three days. The others have more time or less at stake.

en.stem: A complaint says that a hand pump in a village has not worked for a month. Before deciding what to do, what should you find out first?
options: How many hand pumps the district has
Which officer was posted there last year
Whether the pump is in fact out of order, why, and where the village is getting water now
en.why: Defining the problem comes first: the fact, its cause, and the present need. The remedy differs for a broken part, a fallen water level, or a delay in repair.

en.stem: Two clerks can each process 12 applications a day. There are 90 applications, and all must be processed within 3 days. What is the least number of additional clerks, each working at the same rate, needed from the first day?
en.why: Two clerks do 24 a day, or 72 in three days, which is 18 short. One more clerk does 36 in three days. So one additional clerk is enough: 3 × 12 × 3 = 108.
